summary: The Platforms index maps ten source-platform guides to the Bunzai adapter kinds covered on each page. It explains what every guide covers: accepted file shapes, fields represented in Bunzai, same-format field preservation, changes during cross-format conversion, Workbench editing, and common questions. The table lists Agnai characters and lorebooks; Backyard characters; Chub characters and lorebooks; Lumiverse characters, personas, and regex sets; Marinara personas and regex sets; NovelAI lorebooks; Pygmalion characters; RisuAI characters, lorebooks, and regex sets; RoleCall and SillyTavern characters, lorebooks, personas, and regex sets. The Handles column is limited to this guide's coverage and does not claim to inventory upstream platform features. Backyard's flat JSON and .byaf shapes share one page; Marinara character cards use the SillyTavern-shaped path. For unlisted apps, inspect the export; Character Card v2 or v3 JSON is covered by the SillyTavern guide, while other shapes may need another adapter. The generated format reference lists current adapters. Conversion differences are described per page.

sections.title: The platforms
sections.summary: The table maps each platform guide to the Bunzai deck kinds it covers: Agnai characters and lorebooks; Backyard characters; Chub characters and lorebooks; Lumiverse characters, personas, and regex sets; Marinara personas and regex sets; NovelAI lorebooks; Pygmalion characters; RisuAI characters, lorebooks, and regex sets; RoleCall and SillyTavern characters, lorebooks, personas, and regex sets. Handles describes this guide's adapter coverage only; an omitted kind says nothing about the upstream platform's capabilities. Backyard's older flat JSON and modern .byaf character shapes share one page. Marinara character cards use the SillyTavern-shaped path, while Marinara's page covers its persona and regex formats.

sections.title: If your platform isn't listed
sections.summary: Bunzai detects supported files by their contents. If an app exports Character Card v2 or v3 JSON, the SillyTavern guide describes that supported shape. Other exports may need another adapter or may be unsupported, so inspect the file before selecting a target. For the exhaustive generated list of current Bunzai adapters, run bun run bunzai formats or read the format reference. That reference is built from the live adapter registry.

sections.title: Common questions
sections.summary: Why do some platforms list fewer kinds? The table describes only the adapters covered by these guides; it is not an inventory of upstream features. Will a conversion lose anything? Sometimes. Each platform page names the fields that remain or drop, and the converting guide explains the general rule. If an app is not listed, inspect its export or try importing it: Bunzai recognizes supported file shapes rather than relying on app names and reports files it cannot read.
